# 4 Ezra Chapter 16 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 16:6 — rhetorical questions (lion/fire)

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Can-one-drive-away-a-hungry-lion-in-the-forest, or-quench-a-fire-in-the-straw" | Full literal hyphenated |
| LOGOS | "Can one drive away a hungry lion in the forest, or quench a fire in straw" | Same without hyphens; "in straw" |
| PNEUMA | "Can someone drive a hungry lion out of the forest?" | Splits into two questions |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Can one drive away a hungry lion in the forest, or quench a fire in straw when it has once begun to burn?" (LOGOS). Keeping the two images in one sentence preserves the rhetorical accumulation.

---

## 16:11 — "shattered in pieces" vs. "broken in pieces"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "not-be-utterly-broken-in-pieces-at-his-presence" | Literal confringitur |
| LOGOS | "not be utterly shattered at his presence" | "Shattered" is more vivid than "broken in pieces" |
| PNEUMA | "not be shattered to pieces in his presence" | Hybrid |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Not be utterly shattered at his presence" (LOGOS). "Shattered" captures confringitur's violence concisely.

---

## 16:40 — pilgrims on earth

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "be-even-as-pilgrims-upon-the-earth" | Literal peregrini |
| LOGOS | "be even as pilgrims upon the earth" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "live through those coming evils as if you were only passing through on a journey" | Paraphrase loses "pilgrims" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Be even as pilgrims upon the earth" (LOGOS). The word "pilgrims" (peregrini) is theologically rich and should be preserved.

---

## 16:53 — coals of fire on the sinner's head

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "God-shall-burn-coals-of-fire-upon-his-head, which-says-before-the-LORD-God..." | Literal with unusual relative clause |
| LOGOS | "God shall burn coals of fire upon his head, who says before the LORD God and his glory: I have not sinned" | Same, clear antecedent |
| PNEUMA | "God will pour burning coals on the head of anyone who says before the LORD God and his glory: I have not sinned" | "Pour" for "burn"; clearer antecedent with "anyone" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "God shall burn coals of fire upon his head, who says before the LORD God and his glory: I have not sinned" (LOGOS). "Burn coals" is more precise than "pour burning coals"; the relative clause construction, though unusual, mirrors the Latin.

---

## 16:76–78 — closing exhortation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "your-reward-is-beyond-all-measure" | Literal merces multa |
| LOGOS | "your reward is beyond all measure" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "your reward goes beyond all measuring" | "Goes beyond all measuring" slightly more dynamic |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Your reward is beyond all measure" (LOGOS). "Beyond all measure" is a fixed idiom; PNEUMA's variation is acceptable but less elegant.

---

## Total disagreements: 5
